overview: Stabilize the runtime-backed onboarding and control-center foundation in the primary macOS app so the product can register projects, start sessions, and rely on the embedded Python runtime instead of one-off local snapshots.
goals: Finish the runtime-backed onboarding and project registration flow in the Swift app
Harden the embedded Python launcher and runtime service contract
Keep tests, docs, and Xcode project generation aligned with the runtime architecture
nonGoals: Do not introduce any hosted backend or cloud dependency
Do not start the Rust executor implementation in this loop
Do not redesign unrelated UI surfaces outside onboarding and the control center
successMetrics: A bootstrapped repo can be registered and shown in the control center through runtime-backed data
Swift and Python test suites pass for stories that change those surfaces
Architecture docs match the local runtime implementation after each completed story
openQuestions: Should session history UI ship in the same runtime foundation slice or remain deferred after registration and start-session flows are stable?

stack.framework: SwiftUI macOS app with a bundled Python runtime
stack.database: Local file-backed registry under Application Support
stack.auth: No hosted auth in this phase

routes.name: First-run onboarding
routes.purpose: Bootstrap and register a repo, then transition into the runtime-backed control center

routes.name: Control center
routes.purpose: Show the selected registered project, runtime status, and session entry points

uiNotes: The onboarding flow must stay explicit about local-only runtime setup and runtime-backed registration.
The control center should reflect runtime state rather than a stale one-off snapshot.

importFormat.description: Not applicable. This loop works against the existing local macOS app and bundled Python runtime.

rules: The product remains local-first and must not depend on a backend.
Swift is the control plane, Python owns runtime orchestration, and Rust stays deferred as the future trust boundary.
If project.yml changes, regenerate AgentAppFlow.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj with xcodegen instead of hand-editing it.
Each story must preserve focused source control by staging only story-related files and Ralph state files.
qualityGates: Inspect git status before editing and do not mix unrelated dirty files into a story commit
python3 -m pytest python/tests when Python runtime files change
xcodegen generate when Swift sources, project.yml, or the Xcode project need sync
xcodebuild -project AgentAppFlow.xcodeproj -scheme AgentAppFlow -destination 'platform=macOS' test when Swift or Xcode project files change
Update docs when runtime architecture or developer workflow changes

stories.title: Complete runtime-backed onboarding handoff
stories.description: As a first-time AgentAppFlow user, I want onboarding to bootstrap and register a repo into the local runtime so the app transitions directly into the runtime-backed control center.
acceptanceCriteria: FirstRunSetupView completes bootstrap plus registration and hands a project identifier or equivalent runtime-backed selection into the main app flow.
Example: a successful bootstrap/register flow selects the newly registered project and opens the control center with runtime data.
Negative case: if bootstrap or registration fails, the user remains in onboarding and sees an actionable error without a half-completed transition.
Relevant Swift tests cover the onboarding-to-runtime handoff behavior.

stories.title: Harden embedded Python runtime execution
stories.description: As a developer, I want the macOS app to use the bundled Python runtime reliably so runtime commands behave consistently on machines without a user-managed python3 setup.
acceptanceCriteria: BootstrapCLIService and runtime-facing services launch Python through the embedded runtime locator and pass the environment required by the bundled framework.
Example: runtime list/register/start-session flows work when launched through the bundled interpreter path.
Negative case: missing interpreter or runtime launch failure surfaces a structured error rather than failing silently or hanging the UI.
Python tests and relevant Swift tests cover the embedded runtime and runtime-service contract.

stories.title: Align docs and project generation with the runtime foundation
stories.description: As a contributor, I want the architecture docs and generated project files to match the runtime-backed implementation so future contributors and autonomous loops can work from accurate instructions.
acceptanceCriteria: Architecture and onboarding/runtime documentation reflect the local runtime foundation, command surface, and current repo workflow.
Example: docs describe that the control center reads runtime-backed project/session state instead of a one-off snapshot.
Negative case: no documentation or generated project file remains out of sync with project.yml after the story is completed.
If project.yml changes, AgentAppFlow.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj is regenerated with xcodegen and included in the same story.
